metadata.title: fix(ui): set MAX_MEMBERS_PER_TEAM in team forms
metadata.author: gcgoncalves

description:
# 🐛 Bug-fix PR

## 📌 Summary
The "Maximum Members" field in the **Create Team** and **Edit Team** modals has `max="1000"` hardcoded in the HTML. The `MAX_MEMBERS_PER_TEAM` environment variable (default: `100`) is correctly read by the backend but is never surfaced to the admin UI, so:

- When `MAX_MEMBERS_PER_TEAM > 1000`: the form rejects values above 1000, preventing creation of teams larger than 1000 even though the backend allows it.
- When `MAX_MEMBERS_PER_TEAM < 1000`: the form allows values up to 1000, so a non-admin user can set `max_members` well above the configured limit.

Closes #3589

## 🔁 Reproduction Steps
1. Set `MAX_MEMBERS_PER_TEAM=30` in `.env`.
2. Start the app (`make dev`).
3. Log in to the Admin UI as a non-admin user.
4. Navigate to the **Teams** tab → **Create new team**.
5. Set **Maximum Members** to `500` (above the env setting but below 1000).
6. Click **Save**.

**Observed:** Team is created with `max_members=500` — the env cap of `30` is silently bypassed by the UI.

**Alternative path (`MAX_MEMBERS_PER_TEAM > 1000`):**

1. Set `MAX_MEMBERS_PER_TEAM=2000`.
2. Try to set **Maximum Members** to `1500`.
3. Browser rejects the input: "Value must be ≤ 1000".

---

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] For **admin users**, the "Maximum Members" input in the Create Team modal has no `max` attribute.
- [ ] For **non-admin users**, the input has `max` set to `MAX_MEMBERS_PER_TEAM`.
- [ ] The same admin/non-admin distinction applies in the **Edit Team** modal.
- [ ] The default `value` in the Create modal is `min(50, MAX_MEMBERS_PER_TEAM)`.
- [ ] Helper text accurately reflects the limit:
  - Admin: e.g. `"Optional. Admins can set any limit."`
  - Non-admin: e.g. `"Optional, defaults to {MAX_MEMBERS_PER_TEAM}."`
- [ ] Changing `MAX_MEMBERS_PER_TEAM` in the env and restarting reflects the new value without code changes.
- [ ] `min="1"` is preserved on all inputs (regression guard).


## 🐞 Root Cause
Two locations have `max="1000"` hardcoded instead of reading from `settings.max_members_per_team`:

| File | Context |
|------|---------|
| `mcpgateway/templates/admin.html` | Create Team modal — `<input type="number" name="max_members" min="1" max="1000" ...>` |
| `mcpgateway/admin.py` | Edit Team modal — Python f-string: `<input type="number" name="max_members" min="1" max="1000" ...>` |

Additionally, `max_members_per_team` is never passed to the admin template context in `admin.py` (main page render at ~line 3628), so Jinja2 cannot reference it.


## 💡 Fix Description
The "Maximum Members" input in the Create Team and Edit Team modals had max="1000" hardcoded, causing two problems:
- non-admin users could set max_members above `MAX_MEMBERS_PER_TEAM`
- when `MAX_MEMBERS_PER_TEAM` > 1000, the browser rejected valid values

Fix by surfacing the setting to the UI with role-aware behaviour:
- admins: no max attribute (no browser-side cap, matching `max_members` in the backend)
- non-admins: max attribute set to `MAX_MEMBERS_PER_TEAM` (default 100)

The default value in the Create modal is min(50, `MAX_MEMBERS_PER_TEAM`)
so tighter operator-configured limits are respected out of the box.

## 🧪 Verification

| Check                                 | Command              | Status |
|---------------------------------------|----------------------|--------|
| Lint suite                            | `make lint`          |        |
| Unit tests                            | `make test`          |        |
| Coverage ≥ 80 %                       | `make coverage`      |        |
| Manual regression no longer fails     | steps / screenshots  |        |


## ✅ Checklist
- [ ] Code formatted (`make black isort pre-commit`)
- [ ] No secrets/credentials committed

reviews.author: vishu-bh
reviews.body:
Thanks @gcgoncalves to address this issue. The UI change is heading in the right direction and does improve the form behavior, but I found one important gap that still leaves the underlying problem unresolved.

  - High: The current change only fixes the browser-side constraint, not the server-side enforcement. Non-admin users can still bypass the new max attribute by submitting a crafted POST request with a larger max_members value, and the backend
    will accept it. That means the original issue is still present from a security/policy perspective.
    Suggested solution: add backend validation in the create/update team handlers or service layer to enforce settings.max_members_per_team for non-admin users, and only allow values above that limit for admins if that is the intended behavior.
    This should be enforced server-side regardless of what the UI renders.
  - Medium: The PR does not include tests covering the new admin vs non-admin behavior or the original bug scenario. That makes it hard to verify the acceptance criteria and would likely allow regressions later.
    Suggested solution: add tests for both create and edit flows that verify:
      1. non-admin users cannot submit max_members above MAX_MEMBERS_PER_TEAM
      2. admin users can submit higher values if that is expected
      3. the rendered form shows the correct max attribute and helper text for both roles
  - Low: The PR description mentions that the admin UI behavior matches the backend via skip_limits, but in the current implementation that backend flag appears to relate to team-count limits rather than max_members limits. That makes the
    current explanation a bit misleading.
    Suggested solution: update the implementation or the PR description so they are aligned. If admins are meant to bypass MAX_MEMBERS_PER_TEAM, that logic should exist explicitly in the backend; otherwise the description should avoid implying
    that it already does.

  Overall, the UI part looks good, but I think this needs server-side enforcement plus a small test pass before it fully closes the issue.

reviews.body:
this is a solid iteration: the UI fix is good, the role-aware behavior is clearer, and adding server-side checks plus tests is the right direction.

reviews.author: crivetimihai
reviews.body:
Good fix — the hardcoded `max="1000"` was a real bug affecting both directions (non-admins bypassing the cap, admins blocked above 1000).

I rebased onto main (clean, no conflicts) and added three commits on top:

1. **`fix(teams): use extracted is_admin var in update_team, add boundary test`** — `update_team` was re-evaluating `bool(current_user.get("is_admin"))` for `skip_limits` instead of using the `is_admin` variable already extracted two lines above. Also added the missing boundary test for non-admin update at exactly the configured limit (the create path had it, update didn't).

2. **`fix(ui): handle over-limit max_members in non-admin team edit form`** — Edge case: if an admin previously set a team's `max_members` above the configured cap (e.g. 500 when limit is 100), a non-admin opening the edit modal would see `<input max="100" value="500">`, which causes browser validation failure and blocks form submission entirely (can't even edit the team name). Fixed by rendering an empty field with a hint showing the current value and allowed limit. Submitting empty preserves the existing value server-side. Added two regression tests (admin vs non-admin over-limit edit).

3. **`fix(docs): add missing docstring sections in passthrough_headers`** — Unrelated flake8 DAR fixes for `_loopback_skip_set`, `safe_extract_headers_for_loopback`, and `safe_extract_and_filter_for_loopback`.

All tests pass (67 router tests + 3 new admin tests).

commits.message:
fix(ui): handle over-limit max_members in non-admin team edit form

When a non-admin user edits a team whose max_members already exceeds the
configured MAX_MEMBERS_PER_TEAM (e.g. set by an admin), the HTML form
would render value > max, causing browser validation to block submission.

Fix by showing an empty field with a hint displaying the current value
and the allowed limit. Submitting empty preserves the existing value
server-side. Admins continue to see the actual value with no cap.

Add regression tests for both admin and non-admin over-limit edit cases.

Signed-off-by: Mihai Criveti <crivetimihai@gmail.com>
